result.topic_en: Latin notes on the Paris prize problem on heat conduction: after showing that a solution satisfying $\Delta u=0$ and $\Lambda u=\partial u/\partial t$ satisfies the heat equation, section 5 treats the special case (β) in which $\Lambda\Delta u=0$ is independent of $\Delta u=0$, considering an additional linear differential equation $\Theta u=0$ and distinguishing two cases.

items.english: The equation $\Delta u=0$ continues to hold if it holds initially and the function u varies according to $\Lambda u=\partial u/\partial t$. Then it satisfies the law of heat motion, i.e. the equation F=0.
